description: A UNESCO-listed Ottoman-era quarter stacked up a hillside above the harbour, its narrow stepped alleys designed to confuse exactly the kind of outside attack the city faced for centuries - some sections have fallen into disrepair and are structurally unstable, so a local guide who knows which streets are currently safe is worth the small fee.

title: Explore the fortified hilltop ksour of the M'Zab Valley
description: Five walled Mzabite towns built by a breakaway Ibadi Muslim sect a thousand years ago, each stacked in tight concentric rings up to a hilltop mosque for defence - Ghardaïa's design later influenced modernist architects like Le Corbusier, who studied its stark geometric forms directly.

title: Climb the steep sand slope to the Nubian pyramids of Meroe
description: Over 200 steep-sided pyramids built for Kushite kings and queens, smaller and more numerous than Egypt's but almost entirely without other visitors - most were dynamited open in the 1830s by a treasure hunter looking for gold, and the truncated tops seen today are the scars of that destruction, not the original design.

title: Find the lion-headed temple of Naqa in the open desert
description: A Kushite temple complex standing alone in open desert with no modern town nearby, its lion god Apedemak carved onto a temple facade that blends Egyptian, Meroitic and even Roman architectural details - Musawwarat es-Sufra nearby adds a vast elephant-themed temple compound whose exact function is still debated by archaeologists.

title: Climb the sacred mountain of Jebel Barkal above its own pyramid field
description: Ancient Egyptians and Kushites both considered this flat-topped sandstone outcrop the home of the god Amun, building temples and a smaller pyramid field at its base across more than a thousand years of continuous use - the short climb to the summit passes a carved pinnacle rock formation en route.

title: Walk among the pyramids of Nuri, burial ground of Kushite kings
description: The burial site of King Taharqa, who briefly ruled Egypt itself as part of Kush's 25th dynasty, and dozens of later Kushite royals - the pyramids here are older and in some cases larger than Meroe's, yet see even fewer visitors given the extra distance north along the Nile.

title: Watch two rivers of different colour merge at the Nile confluence in Khartoum
description: The Blue Nile, carrying dark silt from the Ethiopian highlands, and the White Nile, running clear from the Central African lakes, are visibly different colours for a stretch after they meet before finally blending - a boat trip out onto the confluence itself shows the colour line far better than either riverbank.

title: Walk the marble streets of Leptis Magna, Rome's best-preserved city
description: Buried under sand for over a thousand years after the city was abandoned, which is why its arch, basilica and harbour survive in a state of preservation that outstrips almost every other Roman site around the Mediterranean - ongoing instability since 2011 has meant most visits happen only through specialist operators who track the security situation district by district.

title: Stand on the stage of the restored Roman theatre at Sabratha
description: A three-tiered Roman theatre facing the Mediterranean, its columned stage backdrop largely reconstructed in the 1930s from original fallen pieces - the wider port city ruins around it show a distinctly Punic layer beneath the Roman one, evidence of Sabratha's earlier life as a Carthaginian trading post.

title: Explore the Greek temples of Cyrene above the Mediterranean cliffs
description: Founded by Greek colonists from Thera in the 7th century BC, its Temple of Zeus larger than the Parthenon in floor area, perched on a plateau above the coast in Libya's less-visited eastern Cyrenaica region - the necropolis carved into the cliffs below holds thousands of rock-cut tombs stretching for kilometres.

title: Walk the covered rooftop passageways of Ghadames' old town
description: A UNESCO-listed oasis town built almost entirely covered against the desert heat, with a separate rooftop level historically reserved for women to move between houses without entering the street below - most families relocated to a modern town nearby in the 1980s, leaving the old town preserved but largely unlived-in.

title: Float in the hypersaline waters of Lake Assal, Africa's lowest point
description: At 155 metres below sea level, it's the lowest point on the African continent and among the saltiest bodies of water on Earth, dense enough to float without effort - salt crust around the shore is still hand-harvested by camel caravan much as it has been for centuries.

title: Search for the endemic Djibouti francolin in Day Forest
description: A relict juniper forest surviving on the cooler upper slopes of the Goda Mountains, the last stronghold of the Djibouti francolin, a bird found nowhere else on Earth and down to a few thousand individuals - the cool highland air is a genuine surprise after the furnace heat of the coast below.

title: Watch sunrise light up the limestone chimneys of Lac Abbé
description: Hundreds of natural limestone chimneys vent steam across a cracked lakebed straddling the Ethiopian border, a landscape so otherworldly it stood in for an alien planet in a Planet of the Apes film - camping overnight near the chimneys for sunrise is the standard way to see them, since the drive out is too rough to attempt twice in a day.

title: Snorkel alongside whale sharks in the Gulf of Tadjoura
description: One of the most reliable places on Earth to swim with whale sharks, which gather here in unusually shallow, calm water to feed on plankton blooms - juveniles dominate the aggregation, and boats are required to keep a minimum distance and cap swimmer numbers per shark to reduce stress on the animals.

title: Walk Asmara's UNESCO-listed Italian Art Deco streetscape
description: Italian colonial planners and architects used 1930s Asmara as a testing ground for modernist and Art Deco design, leaving a concentration of futurist-style buildings - a cinema shaped like an ocean liner, a gas station shaped like an aeroplane - unmatched anywhere else in Africa and largely frozen in place by decades of isolation since.

title: See coral-block Ottoman architecture scarred by war in Massawa
description: A Red Sea port that passed through Ottoman, Egyptian and Italian control before Eritrea's 30-year independence war left visible shell damage on buildings that's never been fully repaired - the coral-block architecture and covered souks show the city's centuries as a trading crossroads despite the scars.

title: Dive centuries-old shipwrecks in the Dahlak Archipelago
description: Over 200 islands off Massawa, most uninhabited, ringed by reefs left largely undived due to decades of restricted access - pearl diving sustained the archipelago's economy for centuries before the trade collapsed, and abandoned pearling-era wells are still visible on some of the larger islands.

title: See 5,000-year-old painted cattle at the Laas Geel rock art site
description: Granite rock shelters near Hargeisa hold some of the best-preserved rock art in Africa, painted by pastoralist herders roughly 5,000 years ago and rediscovered by archaeologists only in 2002 - the vivid ochre and white pigments survived because the shelters' overhangs kept centuries of rain off the painted surfaces.

title: Walk the empty white-sand coastline at Berbera
description: A Red Sea port town with Ottoman and British colonial-era coral-stone buildings and a long, largely undeveloped coastline behind it - decades of low visitor numbers mean the reef offshore has seen little of the damage common to more developed Red Sea coasts elsewhere.

title: See the 13th-century minaret of Mogadishu's Arba'a Rukun Mosque
description: One of the oldest surviving mosques in Mogadishu, its square minaret dated to the 13th century and still standing through decades of civil conflict that destroyed much of the surrounding old city - it stands as one of the clearest physical links to Mogadishu's medieval history as a Swahili coast trading power.
